title: Theo and the Landfall
premise: Paloma Dunmore, a riverboat captain who has spent a lifetime outrunning debts and grief, is stranded in the delta town of Landfall when the monsoon strands her leaking boat, the Kestrel. When an extraordinary low tide exposes a sea cave said to hold the lost inheritance of the drowned shipping magnate Aurelio Voss, Paloma and her young deckhand Theo are pulled into a race against treasure hunters, a corrupt harbormaster, and the calendar itself. With help from Marisol, a cave-diving stranger with her own claim to the Voss name, they must survive the storm season and find proof that the fortune belongs to the drowned town's forgotten families. In the end, Paloma chooses to stop moving: she testifies against the harbormaster, signs the Kestrel's papers over to Theo, and lets Landfall become the first place she's ever stayed.
about_author: Hazel Sandoval is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons working the tidal deltas of the southern coast before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who live on the water because the land never quite made room for them.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Kestrel runs aground on a shifting bar outside Landfall; Paloma reads the water like an old enemy and gets them off, but the hull takes damage she can't afford to fix. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread — every stop costs more than she can pay.

chapters.title: A Town That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While Paloma haggles for repairs, Theo wanders Landfall's flooded market and hears the legend of the Voss cave from a blind storyteller who claims the tide 'opens it once a generation.' Emotional beat: wonder — Theo wants roots; Paloma wants distance.

chapters.title: Harbormaster Bell
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Bell offers to waive the ruinous mooring fees if Paloma ferries 'survey equipment' upriver at night. She refuses, and finds her repair quote mysteriously doubled. Emotional beat: cold recognition of how towns punish outsiders who won't be bought.

chapters.title: The Tide Goes Out Too Far
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. An impossible low tide drains the bay, exposing the mouth of the Voss cave below the cliffs. Theo photographs it; by morning half the town knows. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease as greed gathers on the shore.

chapters.title: Marisol at Low Water
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A stranger in diving gear intercepts them at the cave mouth: Marisol Voss, estranged granddaughter of Aurelio, who says the cave holds documents proving the magnate stole his fleet from indentured crews. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who don't trust anyone.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The three explore the outer chambers at slack tide and find carved crew manifests — names of the stolen. Bell's men spot their lanterns. Emotional beat: history made flesh; the treasure isn't gold, it's evidence.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The season's first great storm traps the Kestrel in harbor with a leaking seam and no dry dock available until the rains end. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the clock is now the enemy, not just Bell.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns why Paloma never stays: a warrant from a port town upriver where she took the blame for a partner's smuggling. Emotional beat: betrayal softening into understanding — her running was survival, not cowardice.

chapters.title: Bell's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Bell corners Paloma: bring him the manifests and he'll bury the warrant. She pretends to consider. Emotional beat: temptation played straight — justice inside the law has never once worked for her.

chapters.title: The Leak Below
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mid-storm, the Kestrel's seam opens properly. Theo and Marisol patch it chest-deep in bilgewater while Paloma holds the boat off the rocks. Emotional beat: terror becoming trust — three strangers functioning as one crew.

chapters.title: Manifests and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals her grandfather disowned her when she asked about the indentured crews; the cave documents name her own grandmother among the stolen. Emotional beat: grief — inheritance can be a debt, not a gift.

chapters.title: The Warrant Catches Up
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A constable arrives on the mail skiff with Paloma's old warrant. Bell smiles from the dock. She surrenders quietly to keep him away from the Kestrel. Emotional beat: sacrifice — she pays for the past so the future stays free.

chapters.title: Holding Cell, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Paloma sits in Bell's jail as the monsoon peaks and the cell floods ankle-deep. Theo organizes the storyteller and market folk to demand her release. Emotional beat: the town choosing sides — belonging arriving unasked.

chapters.title: The Escape at Flood Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Marisol dives the flooded jail's seaward wall and springs Paloma through a maintenance grate as the storm surge peaks. Emotional beat: exhilaration — law failed her; people didn't.

chapters.title: Outlaw Crew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fugitives now, they hide the Kestrel in the mangrove channels and plan one last dive during the storm's eye — the only window before the dry season seals the cave. Emotional beat: defiant calm; outlaws with a purpose.

chapters.title: Bell's Armada
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Bell commandeers two patrol boats to seize the cave 'for safety.' The chase through the flooded mangroves nearly sinks everyone, including Bell's men. Emotional beat: fury tempered by mercy — Paloma saves the men hunting her.

chapters.title: The Eye of the Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Under a freakishly still sky, the three dive the inner chamber and recover the sealed ledgers and Aurelio's confession letter. Bell's boats close in as the eye wall returns. Emotional beat: triumph with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Cave-In
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The returning surge collapses the entrance; Marisol is pinned guiding the ledgers out through a squeeze passage while Bell's men watch, unable to act. Emotional beat: courage at the edge of drowning — she frees herself as the chamber floods.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at the Dock
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cornered on the dock, Paloma doesn't run: she reads the confession aloud to the assembled town as the storm breaks, naming the families owed. Bell's own deputies turn on him. Emotional beat: climax — justice spoken publicly beats justice hidden forever.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rains end. The ledgers go to a judge brought in from upriver; Bell is arrested; the warrant against Paloma is dismissed when her old partner confesses. Emotional beat: exhale — the law, finally, working late but correctly.

chapters.title: Papers Signed in Salt Air
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma signs the Kestrel over to Theo and takes a stake in the restored ferry line serving the cave's new memorial site. Emotional beat: surrender without defeat — letting go of the wheel as an act of love.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, closing. Months later, Theo captains the Kestrel on its first scheduled run while Paloma waits on the dock — staying, waving, home. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging isn't found, it's chosen, and they finally chose it.
